newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SENATE COMMITTEE WANTS THREE TAX BRACKETS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SENATE COMMITTEE WANTS THREE TAX BRACKETS.

text.p: The legislative committe of the Polish Senate, the upper house of parliament, supported the government's plan to keep three tax brackets in 1997, but proposed different tax levels, the Senate press office said.
"The legislative committee supports the government's plan for three tax levels in 1997, but proposed rates of 20, 32 and 44 percent," a official from the press office told Reuters.

Last month the Sejm, the lower house, unexpectedly passed an opposition motion of four personal income tax levels at 17, 20, 33 and 45 percent against a government proposal of 20, 31, 43 percent. This year the tax levels are 20, 33 and 45 percent.

The government called the four bracket plan economically irresponsible and Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko told a senate committe on Wednesday that the government would rather quit than implement new lower tax levels.
The legislative committee is one of two Senate bodies which will decide on whether to alter the lower house's bill before it comes before the full Senate on November 13 or 14.
The Senate's potential changes to the tax law can then be accepted or rejected by the lower house before going to the president who has already announced he would veto a four level tax law.
The legislative committee also called for a further cut in personal income tax levels to 19, 30 and 40 percent in 1998, a official from the committee said.
The official said the other Senate committee deciding the fate of the Sejm tax bill, the National Economy Committee, would likely make up its mind early next week.
